  "text": "In the morning Tobias took the church road home. He had stayed until the woman who arranged the flowers came with her key. Neither asked the other why they were there.

From the road he could see Maren’s door. It was shut. The front window held the pale square of the sky and nothing else.

He went through her gate.

There were eleven posts beside the path. He counted them without meaning to, then kept his hand on the last while he knocked. The wood was rough. A splinter caught beneath his wedding ring.

He called her name once.

Through the window he saw the lamp, unlit, on the sill. Her father’s rug lay straight. Beside the hearth stood the chair in which she mended things, with a stocking turned inside out over its arm.

He had brought no reason to enter. He held to that.

At the gate he stopped to work the splinter free. It was smaller than he expected. He put it in his coat pocket instead of dropping it on the path.

All winter he found it there. Among coins, beneath his folded handkerchief, once caught in the seam. Each time he meant to throw it away when he reached home.

In February a woman asked whether Maren’s house might be let. Her sister needed somewhere quiet.

Tobias said the roof wanted seeing to.

That afternoon he bought a packet of nails. He carried it up the church road, past the turning, and kept it beside his bed.",
